title: sc33/sc34 killed by Windows process-tree termination during orchestrator handoff
scientific_impact: NONE — no final outputs produced, no partial results inspected or used, no seeds or configuration changed

sc33.reason: parent orchestrator termination propagated to child via Windows job/process-group inheritance

sc34.reason: same — sc34 had just been launched by old orchestrator when PID 3360 was terminated

incident_cause: taskkill /F /PID <orchestrator> terminated the Windows process together with its child subprocesses (sc33/sc34 workers) via inherited job-object/process-group handling. Windows does not reliably allow child-process survival across parent termination in this environment.
lesson_learned: On Windows, orchestrator handoffs must occur only at clean points when no worker subprocesses are active. Never attempt mid-run orchestrator replacement while workers are in flight.
recovery_plan: sc33 and sc34 will be rerun from scratch under the final 4-worker launcher (FIRST_SCENARIO=33). This is recovery from an interrupted computation with no prior valid result, not a replicate or post-hoc rerun.
